faqs.question: Hi, what can FRM Genius help me do?
faqs.answer: FRM Genius helps Field Reimbursement Managers detect a payer-policy change, see the territory accounts affected by the resulting conflict, resolve the conflict once at the territory level, and notify the impacted offices of the corrected path.

faqs.question: Why am I seeing a warning about an MMIT update?
faqs.answer: The warning means the synthetic MMIT policy data source was updated and the new value conflicts with an existing policy record for one or more accounts in your territory. Review the alert before the discrepancy causes a treatment-access delay.

faqs.question: Which accounts are affected by the policy change?
faqs.answer: Open the territory impact view from the alert to see the accounts affected by the update. The list shows each account, its plan, the conflicting field, and the previous and updated values.

faqs.question: What changed in the policy record?
faqs.answer: The conflict view compares the old policy value with the new MMIT value so you can see exactly what changed. The source name, last-updated date, plan, and channel are shown alongside the values.

faqs.question: How do I verify where a coverage value came from?
faqs.answer: Use the provenance details displayed with each record. They identify the source, value, last-updated or effective date, plan, and channel so you can understand where the information came from and which accounts it applies to.

faqs.question: Can I resolve the conflict for all affected accounts at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select the territory-level resolve action, review the confirmation step, and choose the true path once. The action updates all affected accounts without requiring you to open them individually.

faqs.question: What happens when I confirm the true path?
faqs.answer: The conflict is cleared for the affected territory accounts, and they return to a resolved state. The resolution is recorded so the action and its supporting source remain visible.

faqs.question: How do I notify every impacted office about the correction?
faqs.answer: After resolving the conflict, use the territory-level notification action to send the corrected path to every impacted account in one motion. The notification includes the supporting source and effective date.

faqs.question: What does the account notification contain?
faqs.answer: The notification is a factual, MLR-safe template describing the corrected path and identifying the source and effective date. It is designed for compliant communication and does not include free-text promotional content.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether the workflow is complete?
faqs.answer: The post-action state shows that the conflicts are cleared, the affected accounts are resolved, and the accounts have been notified. The recorded action and provenance details remain visible for review.

faqs.question: Is this website using real payer or patient data?
faqs.answer: No. The core demonstration uses synthetic data, including a synthetic infused oncology product, payers, plans, accounts, policy records, and the seeded MMIT update.

faqs.question: Does FRM Genius automatically monitor live payer policy pages?
faqs.answer: Live policy monitoring is a stretch goal, not part of the core workflow. The core demonstration injects the synthetic MMIT update as an event; any future public-source monitoring would require provenance capture, source terms review, and legal review.

faqs.question: What should I do if I need additional help?
faqs.answer: Review the source, effective date, plan, channel, and affected-account details shown in the workflow. For assistance beyond the demonstrated scenario, contact your designated support representative.

faqs.question: What do the FRM terms and abbreviations mean?
faqs.answer: FRM means Field Reimbursement Manager. HCP means Healthcare Provider. A payer is the insurance organization covering healthcare costs, and a plan is a specific insurance plan under that payer. A formulary is the list of drugs covered by a health plan; a medical policy contains rules governing a drug's coverage and reimbursement. An account is a hospital, clinic, oncology practice, or healthcare organization managed by an FRM. A territory is the geographic region assigned to an FRM, and lives are the covered members or patients under a plan. PA means Prior Authorization, ST means Step Therapy, and QL means Quantity Limit.

faqs.question: What do the formulary data fields mean?
faqs.answer: Formulary_ID is the unique formulary identifier; Formulary_Name is the formulary name; Payer_Name is the insurance company; Channel is the market segment, such as Commercial, Medicare, or Medicaid; Lives is the covered population; NDC is the National Drug Code; Product_Name is the drug or therapy name; Formulary_Status is the coverage status within the formulary; Restriction identifies coverage restrictions; Tier is the drug placement or tier; Effective_Date is when the policy takes effect; and As_Of_Date is the snapshot or extract date.

faqs.question: What do the medical policy and account data fields mean?
faqs.answer: In the medical policy dataset, Payer_ID and Plan_ID are unique payer and plan identifiers; Plan_Name is the insurance plan; HCPCS_Code is the healthcare billing code; Product_Name is the drug name; Medical_Policy_Number is the policy reference; Coverage_Status shows whether it is covered; PA_Required, Step_Therapy_Required, and Quantity_Limit indicate whether those restrictions apply; Site_of_Care_Restriction lists allowed treatment locations; Bulletin_URL is the source policy document; and Policy_Effective_Date is the policy effective date. In the account dataset, Account_ID is the unique account identifier; Account_Name is the provider organization; Territory is the assigned geographic region; HCP_Specialty is the provider specialty; Primary_Plan_ID and Primary_Plan_Name identify the associated plan; Payer_Name is the payer; and Channel is the market segment.
